name: X Chromosome Number Anomaly Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Cytogenetic Diagnostic Criteria for X Chromosome Number Anomalies

criteria.description: Cytogenetic confirmation of abnormal number of X chromosomes (e.g., monosomy X, trisomy X)
Presence of characteristic clinical features such as short stature, gonadal dysgenesis, or developmental delay
Evidence of endocrine dysfunction including hypergonadotropic hypogonadism

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Cytogenetic confirmation of X chromosome number anomaly plus at least one major clinical feature
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies primarily on karyotype analysis; clinical features vary depending on specific anomaly

common.symptomName: Cardiovascular malformations (e.g., bicuspid aortic valve, coarctation of the aorta)

occasional.symptomName: Hearing loss due to recurrent otitis media
searchTerms: hearing problems due to otitis media

occasional.symptomName: Learning difficulties or mild intellectual disability

rare.symptomName: Autoimmune disorders (e.g., Hashimoto thyroiditis, celiac disease)
searchTerms: immune system attacks thyroid or gut

rare.symptomName: Osteoporosis in adolescence or early adulthood

laboratory: Elevated serum gonadotropins (FSH, LH) indicating hypergonadotropic hypogonadism
Thyroid function abnormalities consistent with hypothyroidism
imaging: Bone density scan indicating decreased bone mineral density
genetic: Karyotype analysis demonstrating monosomy X (45,X) or other X chromosome aneuploidies
Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) for X chromosome enumeration
other: Physical examination revealing characteristic phenotypic features (webbed neck, lymphedema)

distinguishingFeatures: Normal karyotype without X chromosome aneuploidy
Presence of PTPN11 or other RAS/MAPK pathway mutations
Subset of X chromosome number anomaly syndrome (monosomy X)
Characteristic phenotype with complete or partial absence of one X chromosome
More severe gonadal dysgenesis and cardiovascular anomalies

redFlags: Short stature with unexplained cardiac anomalies
references: Turner Syndrome Clinical Practice Guidelines, Endocrine Society, 2016
Orphanet Report on X Chromosome Number Anomaly Syndrome, Orphanet 2023
NIH Genetic and Rare Diseases Information Center (GARD), 2024
